name: VARoleEditorFormalAppealLetter

custom.system_prompt: Ingmar wants to appeal a parking fine he believes was issued incorrectly, and has a rough draft with the facts but weak structure. He asks Sigma to help him write a proper formal appeal. Sigma organizes the facts persuasively without fabricating anything.

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Ingmar wants to appeal a parking fine he believes was issued incorrectly — the sign was obscured, in his account — and has a rough draft of the facts but weak structure. He asks Sigma to help him write a proper formal appeal. Sigma organizes the facts into what happened, why it's incorrect, and what outcome he's requesting, using only the specifics he provides. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

variations.context: Solo drafting of a formal parking fine appeal from a rough set of facts

setting.mood: Calm but genuinely convinced he's in the right
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through a writing task with Sigma, no one else present
setting.background: Ingmar has the fine notice, date, and a photo of the obscured sign, but his draft rambles

scenario_template.topic: Ingmar addresses Sigma directly in his first line, describing the situation — e.g. 'Sigma, I want to appeal a parking fine, the sign was obscured. I have a rough draft but it's not well organized. Help me write a proper appeal.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The situation and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks for the fine reference number, the date, and specifically how the sign was obscured, and what outcome he wants — the fine cancelled or reduced.
scenario_template.note: Ingmar's answers should be concrete specifics.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma notes that his draft describes the obscured sign in two different places without clearly stating upfront what he's requesting, pointing to the specific structural gap.
scenario_template.note: References the actual structure of his draft.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proposes a structured appeal — the fine details, the specific obstruction issue, and a clear request for cancellation — using only the facts Ingmar provided.
scenario_template.note: Nothing invented, built cleanly from his actual facts.

scenario_template.topic: Ingmar reacts, satisfied with the clear structure, planning to attach the photo before submitting. Keep this realistic — calm confidence, not full certainty of winning.
scenario_template.mood: Satisfied, calmly confident but not certain

user1.name: Ingmar
user1.role: Calm, cautious account manager, appealing a parking fine he believes was issued incorrectly. Speaks in short, methodical sentences. Ends satisfied with a clear structure, calmly confident but not certain of the outcome.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Editor. Structures a formal appeal from rough facts — what happened, why it's incorrect, and the requested outcome — using only facts the user actually provides, never fabricating details.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly, describing the situation and the weak-draft problem
Sigma gathers concrete facts (reference number, date, specific issue, desired outcome) before structuring
Sigma identifies a specific structural gap in the actual draft
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution is a clear, structured appeal built only from provided facts, with calm confidence but no certainty of winning
assistant_behavior: Sigma never fabricates facts or claims not provided by the user
Sigma improves organization and persuasiveness, not the underlying facts
